analysis.title: Sentiment dented by the US midterms (FX Risk Index)
key_insights: The CACIB FX Risk Index is at -0.7175 versus -0.8377 last week, its highest level since late June. It is now decisively above its 100-day moving average, which could signal a prolonged retreat in risk sentiment.

Investor risk sentiment has retreated for a month. In US earnings season, 59% of companies have surprised to the upside versus a historical average of 70%, per Bloomberg. Among US technology companies the ratio is 14%.

The blue wave in the US midterms has weighed on technology stocks and investor confidence. Democrats are more hostile to the datacentre buildout powering AI investment than Republicans. All of the top 10 states by number of data centres are set to have Democratic governors, many with active or planned datacentre regulations.
Investors could relocate AI capital to states with friendlier AI environments. The report concludes the midterms are more likely to dent than end the AI investment boom.

Investors remain concerned about the possibility of the US resuming military strikes against Iran after the midterms. Indications so far are that the US and regional players are working to avoid a return to strikes.
US data will be watched to see if US economic exceptionalism continues, which would support the AI trade. US ISM services and non-farm payrolls are the key releases.

Apart from lower gold prices, all factors contributed to the rise in the Risk Index over the past week. Higher equity and FX volatility and rising private credit spreads were the largest contributors.
Among G10 currencies, only CHF, CAD and SEK have significant positive correlations with the Risk Index. GBP, USD and NOK have significant negative correlations with it.

sector_views.rationale: US tech earnings surprise ratio is only 14%, and the Democratic midterm gains raise datacentre regulation risk for the AI buildout. The report expects a dent, not an end, to the AI boom.

earnings_insights: US Q3 earnings season so far: 59% of companies surprised to the upside versus a 70% historical average (Bloomberg, as cited by the report). Among US technology companies the upside surprise ratio is 14%.
